texto:
Sixty days. That's how long a 1973 law gives a president to fight a war without the approval of Congress.

In the Iran war, day sixty was May first. That day, the White House told Congress the hostilities had "terminated."

The law is the War Powers Resolution. President Nixon vetoed it. Congress overrode him, seventy-five to eighteen in the Senate.

Since then, presidents have sent Congress a hundred sixty-eight reports under it. Only one ever started the clock.

Which one? And why has no president done it again? That's in the full file on The American File.

Because the real question was never the sixty days. It's what happens on day sixty.
titulo: A 1973 law gives presidents 60 days of war. Then what? #shorts
descricao: The War Powers Resolution of 1973 set a 60-day clock on wars Congress hasn't approved. Presidents have filed 168 reports under it; only one started the clock. Every number has a source in the full video.
